 Follow Trump Administration Proposes Kicking Even More People Off SNAP Benefits
 Arthur Delaney Mon, November 9, 2026 at 9:53 PM UTC 1 min read Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. Like this article? Keep independent journalism alive. Support HuffPost . 
 The Trump administration has proposed a new eligibility change for food benefits that would cut enrollment by more than 6 million in what would be a dramatic escalation of cuts that already took effect this year.
 The proposed regulation would disallow households from qualifying for Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) benefits based on their receipt of non-cash Temporary Assistance for Needy Families benefits.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The U.S. Department of Agriculture, which runs SNAP, said the proposal would cut off nearly 17% of SNAP households in 2029, or about 3.2 million households containing 6.3 million individuals.
 The big tax cut Trump signed into law last year has already cut SNAP enrollment by 5.5 million individuals -- the sharpest drop in years. More than 36 million Americans still received food benefits from the program as of July, according to the most recent data.
 The first Trump administration made a similar proposal in 2019, only to see it rescinded by President Joe Biden's administration the following year. A similar back-and-forth could occur in 2029 if a Democrat takes the White House that year.
